newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe bourse starts new year at record high.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe bourse starts new year at record high.

text.p: The Zimbabwe Stock Exchange started the first trading day of 1997 on Thurday at a new record high on continuing bullish sentiment underpinned by steady rains over the New Year holiday.
The key 57-share industrial index leapt 53.35 points to close the day at an all time high of 8,839.60.
"As we predicted before the New Year, the market was very firm and we expect it to continue so until there's a dry spell when we should then see a correction," one broker said.
"Sentiment is still very strong as the rains continue to fall and the market should continue firm into next week," ampther broker said.

Among the day's winners, publishing group Zimpapers surged 200 cents to 2,200, horticulture firm Ariston rose 150 cents to 2,450, sugar producer Hippo climbed 25 cents to 1,050 in reasonable turnover, tobacco group TSL added 20 cents to 720 and sugar refinery ZSR gained 10 cents to 1,460.
A few counters bucked the trend with glass firm PG shedding 10 cents to 550 while agricultural group Acacia and pork processor Colcom lost five cents each to 345 and 365 respectively.
Minings were also firm with nickel miner Bindura rising 50 cents to 800 while Wankie Colliery put on 10 cents to 610. Copper producer Mhangura eased five cents to 20.
The secondary mining index rose 29.26 points to end at 1,112.92.
